html:
The Tagish are a First Nations people of the Athabaskan language group who lived around Tagish Lake and Marsh Lake in the southern Yukon, in Canada. They hunted caribou and moose and fished the lakes.

They married heavily with the coastal Tlingit, who controlled the trade passes to the sea, and over time most Tagish took up the Tlingit language and clan system. The Tagish language itself is now nearly gone.

A Tagish man, Keish, known as Skookum Jim, was one of the party that found gold on Bonanza Creek in 1896 and set off the Klondike Gold Rush. The rush brought tens of thousands of outsiders through Tagish land on the trail to Dawson. Most Tagish today belong to the Carcross/Tagish First Nation.
